inputs.modified_text: The owner of Blue Waters has said that Government collects taxes from them “without doing or investing in anything”. While some might view this as an environmental tax, the owner’s complaint really exposes how corporations resist any accountability for the plastic bottles found everywhere, blocking rivers and drains. This is a structural problem where big business externalizes its costs onto the rest of society, piling environmental harm onto vulnerable groups who already face the worst effects of inequality and lack the power to demand better. What we need is real institutional reform so taxes actually force companies to fund protections and cleanup instead of letting profits come before people and the planet.
